description.value: The study examined salience-network activity and directed functional interactions between the dorsal anterior cingulate cortex and bilateral anterior insulae during four perceptual decision-making tasks with varying sensory difficulty.

design.value: Thirty-two participants completed four perceptual decision-making tasks across two MR scanning sessions on different days within a 7-day period. Task difficulty was manipulated by adding noise or varying sensory asynchrony/coherence, and behavioral performance and fMRI BOLD data were collected.

name.value: F.A.C.E. Training-an interactive training by Paul Ekman
performance accuracy

description.value: Accuracy of participants' perceptual decisions in the four discrimination tasks.

name.value: response times

description.value: Time taken to report perceptual decisions, recorded outside the scanner.

name.value: task difficulty

source_definition.value: Noise level, sensory ambiguity, audiovisual asynchrony versus synchrony, or random-dot-motion coherence used to vary perceptual difficulty.

levels.value: 0%, 40%, and 55% noise; 0% and 40% noise; synchrony and asynchrony; 100%, combined 12% and 20% color coherence, and combined 12% and 20% color incoherence

name.value: human participants

description.value: There were 32 human participants (16 males, 16 females; mean age±standard deviation=27.6±4.7 years) who completed all four experimental tasks. One more male participant took part in face-house discrimination and in audiovisual asynchrony and synchrony perception tasks.

acquired_count.value: 32 completed all four experimental tasks; one additional male participated in two tasks

inclusion_criteria.value: normal or corrected to normal vision

exclusion_criteria.value: No participant reported difficulties recognizing red and green dots during practice session hence no red/green color blindness was reported.

task_description.value: Participants discriminated face and house images degraded with 0%, 40%, or 55% noise.

instructions.value: Indicate whether the presented picture was a house or face as quickly and as accurately as possible.

stimuli.value: 14 images of faces and 14 images of houses, equalized for luminance and degraded by image pixel phase randomization with Gaussian noise at 0%, 40%, and 55%.

task_description.value: Participants discriminated happy and angry human face images presented as clear or noisy stimuli.

instructions.value: Indicate whether the presented face was happy or angry.

stimuli.value: Two sets of human face images, a happy set and an angry set, with eight images per set; clear images had 0% noise and noisy images had 40% noise.

task_name.value: audio-visual asynchrony and synchrony perception task

task_description.value: Participants judged whether paired auditory and visual stimuli were synchronous or asynchronous.

instructions.value: Report whether the auditory and visual stimuli were perceived as synchronous or asynchronous.

stimuli.value: A 440-Hz, 30-ms tone paired with a 30-ms yellow-red disc flash; audiovisual asynchrony was varied around the individual's threshold for simultaneity.

task_name.value: random dot motion direction discrimination task

task_description.value: Participants discriminated leftward versus rightward motion in noisy random-dot fields with varying coherence and color coherence.

instructions.value: Report whether the dots moved to the left or right.

stimuli.value: Randomly moving noisy fields of red and green dots. Coherence levels were 12%, 20%, and 100%, in color coherence and color incoherence conditions.

instrument.value: 3-Tesla Siemens scanner available at the Georgia State University and Georgia Institute of Technology Center for Advanced Brain Imaging

description.value: Whole-brain MRI data were acquired using T2*-weighted gradient echo-planar imaging. Functional scans had TE=30 msec, TR=2000 msec, flip angle=90°, voxel size=3×3×3 mm3, field of view=204×204 mm, matrix size=68×68, and 37 axial slices each of 3 mm thickness.

High-resolution anatomical images were acquired for anatomical references using a magnetization-prepared rapid gradient-echo sequence with TR=2250 msec, TE=4.18 msec, flip angle=9°, inversion time=900 msec, and voxel size=1×1×1 mm3.

MRI data were analyzed using SPM8 and underwent slice timing correction, motion correction, coregistration to the individual anatomical image, normalization to the Montreal Neurological Institute template, and spatial smoothing of the normalized image with an 8-mm isotropic Gaussian kernel.

software.value: Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM8; Wellcome Trust Center, London)

steps.value: normalization to Montreal Neurological Institute template
spatial smoothing with an 8-mm isotropic Gaussian kernel
hemodynamic deconvolution of ROI BOLD time series

model_settings.value: At the first level, a separate GLM was specified according to task sequences and behavioral responses for each participant. Correct trials for each condition, rest, and six motion parameters were included; motion parameters were nuisance covariates. Individual contrast images were entered into a second-level separate one-sample t-test.

estimator.value: one-sample t-test at the second level

model_settings.value: Deconvolved ROI time series were modeled using parametric Granger causality spectra. The optimal autoregressive model order was selected by comparing parametric and nonparametric power spectra. Time-domain values were obtained by integrating causality spectra over the entire frequency range. Conditional Granger causality was used to rule out mediated interactions.

estimator.value: random permutation surrogate thresholding with a minimum of 1000 random permutations; gamma-distribution threshold at p<10−3
